summary.text: Emily Dievendorf is a Democratic member of the Michigan House of Representatives from District 77 who has served since January 1, 2023, and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
Before holding office Dievendorf worked as a legislative staffer and as policy director and manager of Equality Michigan, according to a Ballotpedia survey.

paragraphs.text: Dievendorf lives in Lansing and earned a bachelor's degree in social relations from Michigan State University.

In a 2022 Ballotpedia survey, Dievendorf said they had worked in the Michigan House for Democratic legislators for nearly a decade, including as chief of staff to Representative Andy Coulouris, before becoming policy director of Equality Michigan in 2010 and managing the organization until 2015.

The survey also says Dievendorf was appointed to the Michigan Advisory Committee to the U.S. Commission on Civil Rights in 2015, worked as an independent political and civil rights consultant, and co-founded a nonprofit bookstore in downtown Lansing.
Dievendorf succeeded Republican Tommy Brann in District 77 and in 2025-2026 serves on the House Agriculture and Regulatory Reform committees.
Dievendorf advanced from the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary and faces Republican Sally Jo Nelton and Libertarian Jennifer Long in the general election on November 3, 2026.
In the 2022 survey, Dievendorf named a living wage, equitable public school funding and addressing gun violence among the main points of the campaign.
